title: Modi Uses Somnath Stage to Skewer Nehru, Congress
excerpt: PM marks 75 years of temple's reconstruction, accuses opposition of choosing appeasement over national self-respect
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi stood before tens of thousands at Gujarat's Somnath Temple on May 11 and used India's most storied pilgrimage site to deliver one of his sharpest attacks on the Congress party's founding legacy.

**What happened at Somnath:**
Modi addressed the Somnath Amrut Mahotsav — marking 75 years since the reconstructed Jyotirlinga was consecrated in 1951 — and praised Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and first President Dr. Rajendra Prasad for championing the temple's restoration after Independence. He then turned to Nehru, telling the crowd: 'But we all know how much opposition they faced from Nehru Ji.' Modi released a commemorative stamp and coin to mark the anniversary.

**The political charge:**
Without naming Congress directly, Modi drew a straight line from Nehru's resistance to what he called forces that still 'prioritise appeasement over national self-respect.' He extended that critique to the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, noting that 'opposition was raised even against it.' The speech fits a consistent BJP pattern of contrasting Patel's civilisational assertiveness with Nehru's secularist caution — a contrast that sharpens before every election cycle. Modi also noted that May 11 carries added weight as the anniversary of India's 1998 nuclear tests.

**Context and BJP strategy:**
Modi framed the Somnath Amrut Mahotsav as 'a festival of inspiration for India for the next thousand years,' tying it to a string of temple-corridor projects — Kashi Vishwanath Dham, Mahakal Mahalok, and Kedarnath — that his government has driven since 2014. Historians note that Nehru's private letters did express discomfort with government association with the 1951 consecration on secularist grounds, giving Modi a documented record to cite.

**What to watch:**
Congress has yet to formally respond; its counterargument — that Nehru backed the Trust model rather than government funding — will test whether the party can reclaim the Patel-Prasad narrative before the next state polls.
